subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that cos(π/9) cos(2π/9) cos(3π/9) cos(4π/9) = 1/16.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 39(iv), book p.92. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The two marks sit on applying the product identity and on the closing multiplication; separating the cos(π/3) factor stays on the page as unmarked working. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1-Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, and Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations holds two of those ten slots. NUMERIC CHECK before authoring: the product was evaluated to 12 decimal places as 0.062500000000, which is exactly 1/16. PRINTED CLAIM CHECKED AND FOUND CORRECT: 3π/9 = π/3, so that factor is exactly 1/2 and the printed 1/16 could have been a lost or doubled factor of 2. It is not. The other three angles 20°, 40°, 80° form the standard product cos A cos(60° − A) cos(60° + A) = (1/4) cos 3A, which is (1/4) cos 60° = 1/8, and 1/2 × 1/8 = 1/16. The numeric evaluation above agrees, so the stem was authored as printed with no repair. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Separate the cos(π/3) factor
steps.margin_note: 3π/9 cancels to π/3 = 60°, whose cosine is 1/2. Pull that out and convert the other three angles to degrees.

recall.must_convey: That cos(3π/9) = cos 60° = 1/2 is taken out, leaving cos 20° cos 40° cos 80°.
accept: three pi by nine is pi by three so that factor is one half
take out cos sixty which is a half
the other angles are twenty forty and eighty degrees
three pi by nine ante sixty degrees, adi half

steps.why: The third factor is a known value on its own, so it is taken out first. What is left is a three-factor product in 20°, 40° and 80°.
common_mistakes: Leaving cos(3π/9) inside and looking for a four-angle pattern.
steps.memory_tip: 3π/9 is π/3, and cos 60° = 1/2. Take it out before doing anything else.

steps.label: Apply the product identity
steps.margin_note: First mark. Quote the identity, then put A = 20° so that 3A = 60°. Three unknown cosines become one known cosine.
lines: cos A cos(60° − A) cos(60° + A)

recall.must_convey: That cos A cos(60° − A) cos(60° + A) = (1/4) cos 3A, so with A = 20° the product is (1/4) cos 60°.
accept: cos a cos sixty minus a cos sixty plus a is one by four cos three a
with a as twenty the angle three a is sixty
the three cosines give a quarter of cos sixty
a equal twenty pettithe three a sixty avthundi
use the triple angle product identity
reject: the answer is one by sixteen

steps.why: The identity replaces three cosines of awkward angles by a single cosine of 3A. With A = 20° that single angle is 60°, whose value is known.
common_mistakes: Using the sine identity (1/4) sin 3A by mistake.
steps.memory_tip: The three angles A, 60° − A, 60° + A give a quarter of cos 3A.

steps.label: Multiply by cos(π/3)
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Bring back the 1/2 separated at the start. 1/8 of that is 1/16, and the extra halving is the whole reason the answer is not 1/8.

recall.must_convey: That cos 20° cos 40° cos 80° = 1/8 and the separated 1/2 halves it to 1/16.
accept: a quarter of a half is one by eight
then multiply by the half taken out at the start
one half into one by eight is one by sixteen
modati lo teesina half tho multiply cheyyali
the answer is one by sixteen
reject: use the triple angle product identity

steps.why: The three-factor product is 1/8, and the cos(π/3) taken out at the start contributes the extra 1/2. Missing that factor would give 1/8 instead of 1/16.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the 1/2 taken out at the start and answering 1/8.
Adding the two fractions instead of multiplying them.
steps.memory_tip: The identity gives 1/8, and the cos(π/3) taken out at the start halves it again to 1/16.
